target_customer: Korean startups (freemium cap table, paid by number of stakeholders), plus venture investors who pay by fund AUM and portfolio count
problem: Korean startups and investors managed cap tables, stock options and investor reporting in Excel and older ERP tools, with no standard for securities data.
business_model: B2B SaaS, freemium for startups priced by stakeholders, subscription for investors priced by fund AUM and number of portfolios
product_category: Equity management and cap table software, fintech

founders.name: Andy Choi
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked as a software engineer in Silicon Valley and as a VC in Korea. Employers and education not named in sources opened.

founders.name: Dan Hong
founders.background_notes: Named as a former VC co-founder by TechCrunch, August 2022.

founders.name: Pilseon Jun
founders.background_notes: Named as a former VC co-founder by TechCrunch, August 2022.

competitors.name: Carta
competitors.what: US cap table and equity management platform that the press later called the model QuotaBook followed

technical_complexity.rationale: Cap table, option and governance workflows are standard SaaS engineering, but modelling Korean securities and corporate law and syncing investor data added domain difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Once a startup holds its ownership records and investor consents in the system, switching is costly. Korean securities rules made a direct copy of a US product impractical (per a press profile). TechCrunch reported about 40 percent of Korean startups on the cap table service by August 2022.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of a larger player copying or buying it by 2022. Carta Ventures was an investor in the June 2021 round.

market_need_then: Startups used Excel and older ERP tools for equity records (TechCrunch, August 2022). Korea had a growing venture ecosystem with no dominant local cap table standard.

branding.domain_note: Uses quotabook.com; no acquisition history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: formal fintech positioning: standardizing securities administration

brand_strength.rationale: No source on brand assets or community. Press later referred to the company as QuotaLab (parent Quota Lab, Inc.), a naming split between company and product.

outcome_analysis: QuotaBook was founded in 2019 by former VCs in Seoul, joined YC in Winter 2021, raised a round in June 2021 and an $11 million round in August 2022, and by then claimed about 40 percent of Korean startups on its cap table product. The domain insight of ex-investors and the switching costs of holding ownership records explain the traction. The company is still active and no outcome beyond growth is public.
notes: Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. Aggregators call the 2022 round Series A, one press report calls it Series A2. Total raised is about 20 million per TechCrunch and press, CB Insights shows 16.98 million, a conflict. The June 2021 round amount is not stated in the sources opened. Competitor list is thin: TechCrunch names no direct rival, and the Carta source is dated 2022, well after the batch, so treat it as weak. Founder education and prior employers not found. Name origin not found; a branding search returned nothing about the company.
